subject: Request: Uptime credit attribution after Bridge-node failover
messages:
From: Clare Bishop <support@clearmeridian.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed partial degradations 2027-06-09 — asking for SLA apportionment

Hi Karthik,

We observed several 5–15 second tail-latency spikes and an elevated error rate on our production traffic between 2027-06-09T23:44:00Z and 2027-06-09T23:58:00Z (UTC). Our synthetic transaction monitors show 18 failures and sustained 20% latency regression vs baseline.

Attached are our synthetic transaction logs and the timestamps mapped to our customers. Based on the SLO window in our contract, we believe this qualifies as a partial degradation and would like to request an uptime credit review.

We noticed a CloudTransit maintenance notice that mentions a bridge-node failover overlapping our window; we need Redwood’s view on whether that third-party event should be excluded from the uptime calculation or apportioned.

Can you please:
- Confirm Redwood’s observed request-level failures and tokenized probe failures for the same interval
- Explain whether the bridge-node failover meets the contract’s third-party exclusion language
- Provide the next steps and an estimated timeline for a credit decision

Thanks,
Clare Bishop
Head of Platform Reliability
ClearMeridian
Attachment: clearmeridian_synthetic_transactions_2027-06-09.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Clare Bishop <support@clearmeridian.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>, CloudTransit Ops <ops@cloudtransit.example>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed partial degradations 2027-06-09 — asking for SLA apportionment

Hi Clare — thanks for the heads up and for sending the transaction CSV. I’ve pulled our probe traces and initial token-level metrics for the window you called out and attached the Redwood probe dump.

Quick answers up front:
- We see elevated 5xx rates and increased p50/p95 latency in the same UTC window; our front-door probes show an uptick in 504/502 errors beginning at 23:45:10Z and a return to baseline at ~23:57:30Z.
- CloudTransit (cc’d) indicates there was a bridge-node maintenance/forced failover in that region during the period; we need their syslog and maintenance SLA language to determine how much, if any, should be excluded.

Next steps from our side:
1) Olga, can you correlate the probe traces with the serving-side KV eviction logs and KV cache miss rate? Focus on 23:40–24:05Z UTC.
2) Marissa, please coordinate with CloudTransit on whether the maintenance meets the contract’s third-party exclusion criteria.
3) Clare, once we have vendor evidence and our correlated logs, I’ll propose an apportionment calculation (vendor vs Redwood responsibility) and a draft credit amount.

Estimated timeline: initial internal correlation by EOD tomorrow (2027-06-11), vendor evidence by EOD 2027-06-12, consolidated decision by 2027-06-15.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_probe_logs_2027-06-09.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed partial degradations 2027-06-09 — asking for SLA apportionment

Karthik — thanks for the quick triage. Logging notes below and direction on apportionment approach.

Summary of findings so far (internal):
- Redwood probes show a 12-minute elevated error window matching ClearMeridian’s timestamps. Token-level traces indicate an increased retry rate and a cluster-level failover event in front-door routing.
- Preliminary serving logs show a spike in KV misses starting 23:46Z and peaking at 23:50Z; multiple downstream retries were observed.

Policy guidance: because the incident timeline overlaps a CloudTransit bridge-node failover, we need to determine whether the failover is a Redwood-controlled event or a third-party maintenance that meets the contract’s exclusion clause. If CloudTransit initiated planned maintenance (with advance notice per their contract), we should consider apportionment/exclusion per section 4.2; if the bridge node failed without notice, it’s more likely to be apportioned.

Olga — please prioritize a join of the KV eviction timelines with our client-level error traces and produce the initial uptime math (minutes of customer-facing degradation attributed to Redwood vs vendor). Put the output in initial_uptime_calc_2027-06-11.csv. Include assumptions and the bucket boundaries (full outage vs partial degradation).

I will own outreach to legal for contract language mapping and will follow up with CloudTransit.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
Attachment: initial_uptime_calc_2027-06-11.csv
From: CloudTransit Ops <ops@cloudtransit.example>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Cc: Clare Bishop <support@clearmeridian.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed partial degradations 2027-06-09 — CloudTransit bridge-node notice + syslog

Hi all — CloudTransit here. Confirming that on 2027-06-09 at 23:44:55Z we performed a forced bridge-node failover in us-west-2 as part of emergency automated remediations. There was no customer-facing advance notice due to the automated nature of the remediation.

We’re attaching the maintenance notice and the node syslog showing the failover and subsequent rehoming of sessions. Our telemetry indicates a 10–14 minute window where the bridge node was completing handoff; some upstream connections saw transient 502/504 responses.

Per our vendor SLA, we accept partial responsibility for service impact stemming from bridge-node failovers but reserve that exclusion/apportionment to events initiated by us when they were within our control. Based on our timeline and internal tracing, CloudTransit recommends a 60% vendor responsibility apportionment and 40% Redwood responsibility for the customer-facing disruption.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the logs.

— CloudTransit Ops
Attachment: cloudtransit_maintenance_notice_2027-06-09.pdf
Attachment: cloudtransit_syslog_2027-06-09.txt
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Clare Bishop <support@clearmeridian.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>, CloudTransit Ops <ops@cloudtransit.example>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Final: proposed apportionment and next steps for ClearMeridian SLA credit

Hi Clare — quick summary and the proposed path forward. Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround.

What we found:
- Incident window: 2027-06-09T23:44:55Z–2027-06-09T23:57:30Z (13m35s).
- Redwood probe/serving correlation: ~8m20s of customer-facing elevated error/latency that align to KV cache miss/retries.
- CloudTransit evidence: forced bridge-node failover with 10–14 minute handoff; vendor acknowledges they initiated the remediation without advance notice.

Proposed apportionment (per vendor recommendation and our internal correlation):
- CloudTransit responsibility: 60% of the measured customer-impact window
- Redwood responsibility: 40% of the measured customer-impact window

Proposed credit calculation: we will calculate the credit against the impacted SLO window using the apportioned downtime minutes (total measured impact * Redwood responsibility). I’ve attached the initial uptime calc CSV and a link to the evidence folder.

Next steps:
1) Clare — please confirm you accept the 60/40 apportionment. Once confirmed, we’ll generate a formal credit memo and route it for finance approval (target completion 2027-06-18).
2) CloudTransit — please confirm in writing you agree to the 60% assignment so we can include it in the formal memo.
3) Legal/Finance — Marissa will route the final memo for sign-off; we’ll include CloudTransit evidence and ClearMeridian’s logs.

If you’d prefer a short call to finalize, I can set one up tomorrow morning PT.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: initial_uptime_calc_2027-06-15.csv
